To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) all four species of finch tested here regress their gonads in late summer/autumn and initiate prebasic molt; (2) Cassin's finch, a species with a strict seasonal breeding schedule, did not respond to a long day stimulus in autumn; and (3) the remaining species, which have more flexible reproductive schedules, did respond to the long day stimulus.

(1) absolute photorefractory period length is not fixed within a species, (2) absolute photorefraction period length varies with latitude, and (3) absolute photorefraction period length is correlated with the time of onset of photorefractorines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the adaptive significance of the annual change in day length (photoperiod) in seasonally breeding birds.
how photoperiodic response is regulated by the brain and how this regulation affects the timing of reproduction in birds.
the evolution of photoperiodic response systems in birds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adaptive nature of absolute photorefactoriness remains unresolved.

absolute photorefractorness is not an obligate component of photoperiodic response mechanisms in all species of carduelines, but it may be a necessary component of the photoperiodic mechanism of some species.
photorefractorily is not a universal feature of the photoperiod response of seasonally breeding birds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adaptive specialization hypothesis is not supported for all seasonally breeding species.
absolute photorefractory systems are more widespread in the Carduelini than previously thought.
the species that exhibit absolute photorefactoriness in the fall are the species with a more predictable breeding season and a more reliable resource supply.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photorefractorine state of a species is not necessarily fixed.
absolute photorefractivity is not a universal characteristic of all seasonally breeding birds.
absolute photorefractory responses are not a necessary component of a seasonally breeding life history.
